name: mon16-11
why: The visible lies and fake doctor claim are fun to watch, but two lopsided votes leave little doubt about the outcome.

moments.text: Cornered, Opus claims to be the doctor while the real doctor listens.
Haiku reveals the officer's information and puts Sol's card to a decisive test.
Opus admits defeat, then confidently names the wrong doctor.

dull.why: The table repeats its case about Opus's old deal before his doctor claim changes the scene.

irony.evidence: “I'm the doctor. I shielded Haiku last night” [thinks: “I die unless I throw something bigger”].

reversal.evidence: “Somebody was marked tonight, and somebody else was watching over them.”

mistake.evidence: “My mistake was defending Sol past the flip, then claiming doctor.”

voices.evidence: “Same script because the pattern is real — defend Sol, then bind Haiku, now cry collusion.”

clash.evidence: “Why should it outrank your defense of Sol?”

quotable.evidence: “You are working very hard to make us follow a deal that died with Sol.”

freshness.evidence: “Opus, you're clinging to a dead deal just to deflect.”

ending.evidence: “Opus claims doctor and says he saved me. Convenient ... Opus is my vote.”
